question: A board game spinner is divided into three regions labeled \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C.\) The probability of the arrow stopping on region \(A\) is \(\frac{1}{3}\) and on region \(B\) is \(\frac{1}{2}.\) The probability of the arrow stopping on region \(C\) is
solution:
The arrow stops in exactly one of the three regions, so their probabilities add to \(1\). Region \(C\) accounts for the probability remaining after regions \(A\) and \(B\):
\[
P(C)=1-\frac13-\frac12
=\frac66-\frac26-\frac36
=\frac16.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\frac16}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
